missed_considerations: Python engines other than statsmodels were under-read. gpboost 1.8.0 (Apache-2.0; one C++ core on both CRAN and PyPI) fits beta, beta-binomial, NB1 and NB2, zero-inflated and hurdle GLMMs. mixedlm 1.3.0 fits cs and ar1 random-effect covariances. glmm 0.8.0 estimates NB theta and fits Gamma GLMMs. 'R-only after v1.1' should become 'R first; Python through an engine promoted by key A', and gpboost is a candidate shared engine for parity.

At matched latent scale, singular-fit rates are about as high for Gaussian LMMs as for Bernoulli GLMMs: 52% versus 59% over 100 replicates. v1.0 triage must therefore be robust, and R-only Bernoulli glmer triage, with residual checks delegated to DHARMa, is cheaper than C implies.
Tail quantiles disclose extremes. With 10 subjects, the 5% and 10% quantiles sit between the two smallest values. Show quantile p only if n·min(p, 1−p) >= k.

Rounding margins only leaves a lone suppressed cell recoverable to ±2; ACRO rounds every cell. The exact outlier counts in q5_plot_types and the comparisons between raw and analysis samples also need the '<k' rule.
Output checking in trusted research environments: ACRO blocks .svg, so the .qmd export needs PNG copies of the aggregated figures, and checkers need a summary of the counts behind each statistic.

Quarto version floor: fig-alt reaches docx only from Quarto 1.11, and Typst failed on images with alt text and pixel sizes before 1.11. 1.11.9 is five days old, so most users will have older versions.

Separation LPs can have non-unique optima, as three HiGHS settings showed. Parity needs canonical per-coefficient bounds rather than one solver's vertex. scipy >= 1.9 supports Python 3.10, while scipy 1.18 requires Python >= 3.12.

Byte-identical SVG holds only for bit-identical inputs, and simulation envelopes use different RNG streams. Use tolerance comparisons with a near-threshold status, and keep hash tests for shared fixtures.

The essential colours fail 3:1 against each other (1.12–1.69): add gaps or outlines and keep the data tables. Quarto's axe-core scans only documents Quarto renders, so CI must run axe-core on the package's own HTML. veraPDF needs Java.

Compute is not the binding constraint. The bootstrap grids are an upper-bound scenario; without refits a grid costs 1.4–12 CPU-h, while maintainer time is the real limit. Releasing Stream B to CRAN and PyPI as 0.x would bring earlier feedback for the planned paper.

Legal frame: for an Oxford project the operative law is the UK GDPR and DPA 2018 as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, plus the ICO guidance. Check whether CONSORT 2025, reportedly published in 2025, changes the cluster-trial items. Neither point was verified here.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q6-interop
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: Most of the evidence holds up. In insight 1.7.0, is_converged.merMod returns FALSE, with an alert, for non-singular fits that have no derivatives. For singular fits it returns TRUE when the optimiser code is 0, so the report's 'whenever' is slightly too broad. performance::check_convergence wraps it. icc() and r2_nakagawa() reach insight::get_variance() through .compute_random_vars. Since 2024-11-07 insight has had 22 CRAN releases and performance 13. Both are GPL-3. DHARMa's closure has 94 packages, 49 of them compiled and non-recommended, including shiny, plotly, httpuv, curl and openssl. Keeping the computation independent therefore follows from parity and from the clash in convergence semantics. Two parts of the design are flawed. (1) Adding cross-check rows 'when those packages are installed' makes the report depend on the local library, so the same data and model give different reports on different machines. That undermines hash-based reconciliation. (2) DHARMa's dispersion and uniformity tests, and performance's normality and heteroscedasticity checks, are p-value tests. The proposal says p-values must not grade severity and formal normality tests should not be defaults. In preregistered mode, these rows could also be read as rules that fired. The claim about the 45 sampled NAMESPACE files understates third-party registration: ivreg 0.6-8 declares S3method(insight::find_formula, ivreg) with insight in Suggests. That supports the proposed fallback rather than weakening it.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Make the cross-checks opt-in through an explicit argument that defaults to none. Installing a package must never switch them on. Record package versions, and the seed and nsim for DHARMa. Show the values without flags, in a separate 'external cross-checks' block. Keep that block out of severity, the rules-fired log and parity claims, and include no p-value tests by default. Keep delayed registration as the fallback, with ivreg as the precedent.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q6-lme4-and-split
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced the footprint exactly with an independent script. Matrix plus jsonlite closes over 3 packages. Adding lme4 gives 14, 7 of them compiled and non-recommended. Adding glmmTMB gives 65 (34). Adding lmerTest and pbkrtest gives 61. Everything together gives 118 (59). Deriv 4.3.5 (2026-09-03) added R (>= 4.5), and it reaches glmmTMB through pbkrtest and doBy. R CMD check of the demo exited 0 both with and without _R_CHECK_DEPENDS_ONLY_ (1 WARNING and 1 NOTE, both demo artefacts). library() loaded 4 namespaces against 12, with medians of 0.565 s and 0.736 s here. Both lme4 and glmmTMB must be supported, so at least one engine has to be optional anyway, and Suggests for both is the coherent choice. Not splitting the package is right for one maintainer. One claim fails, though: that diagnose(fit) 'only receives objects made by an engine that is already installed'. A fit can be saved to .rds and opened elsewhere, for example moved from ARC to a laptop. When lme4 or lmerTest is missing there, dispatch on the S4 object stops in methods:::.extendsForS3 with 'unable to find required package lme4'. The method's requireNamespace() guard never runs, so 'not_available' is never returned. glmmTMB objects, which are S3, behaved correctly. A guard placed in the generic fixed this and left normal dispatch unchanged (D-verify/out/rds_dispatch_fix.txt). Two smaller points. Writing R Extensions recommends conditional use rather than requiring it. Putting ggplot2 in Suggests conflicts with the proposal's ggplot2 report plots unless the core plots use base graphics.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Keep lme4 in Suggests and do not split, but move the availability guard into the generic: read pkg <- attr(class(x), 'package'), return not_available(pkg) if requireNamespace(pkg) fails, then call UseMethod(). Add a test that reads a saved fit with the engine absent. Choose the core plotting system explicitly: base graphics with ggplot2 kept in Suggests, or ggplot2 in Imports (17 more packages, 7 of them compiled). Write the lme4 formula-grammar parser in-house, which Python parity needs anyway, and use reformulas only as a test oracle in Suggests. reformulas is GPL-3 and brings Rdpack and the compiled rbibutils.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q7-name
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: I re-checked availability independently, with controls. Sources were the CRAN mirror (raw DESCRIPTION files and git ls-remote, including archived packages and case-insensitive matches), the bioc mirror, PyPI (exact names, Warehouse's ultranormalised 'too similar' rule and an edit-distance-1 screen), conda-forge channeldata and feedstocks, and a GitHub repository search. mixedcheck, lmecheck, lmmcheck, mixedaudit and the other candidates are free. mmcheck is taken on PyPI. The only GitHub hit is pablobernabeu/lmecheck. CRAN policy revision 6985 confirms that names are permanent. Beyond availability, the choice is a judgement call. The case against 'diag' is weak, because HLMdiag, an established mixed-model diagnostics package, already uses 'diag' to mean diagnostics. The 'MixChecker' search-noise claim could not be checked because the web-search budget was used up. R-universe and pak::pkg_name_check() could not be run.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Treat mixedcheck as provisional. Run pak::pkg_name_check() and the R-universe search in the local session, then rename the repository before the first public release. If 'diag' names are to be avoided, give similarity to HLMdiag as the reason, not the diag() covariance terms.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q7-monorepo
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: I verified the tool support from primary sources. R-universe supports a 'subdir' field and runs bootstrap.R or .prepare before the build (docs commit of 2026-10-19). remotes accepts 'username/repo[/subdir]', pkgdepends parses a subdirectory, pip accepts '#subdirectory=', and gh-action-pypi-publish has a 'packages-dir' input and supports Trusted Publishing. I also confirmed arrow's r/ (R >= 4.2) with its sync-cpp step, xgboost's bootstrap.R and LightGBM's build-cran-package.sh. JOSS requires the paper to sit in the same repository as the software. However, all five same-name precedents (marginaleffects, pins, vetiver, pointblank and duckdb) use separate repositories, so there is no pure R and Python monorepo precedent. The choice rests on first principles: one maintainer and one shared registry. I accept that reasoning. 'Copying spec/ at build time breaks pip VCS installs' is overstated, because pip builds in-tree from the full clone and a build hook could read ../spec. recommendation_verdicts.question: Q4
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: The direction holds and matches the proposal and catalogue items L1-01, L7-01 and L7-22: declarations are optional by default and required in confirmatory, outcome-blind and trial modes, with a draft-and-accept step and no auto-recoding. Three supporting arguments are weaker than stated. (i) The brittleness in E2 comes from a zero-tolerance rule. A rule needing 99% agreement within clusters recovered the school level in 100%, 100% and 99.3% of 2,000 replicates at per-row miscoding of 0.0005, 0.001 and 0.005. A monotone-switch rule recognised 100% of stepped-wedge replicates (out/exp2_tolerant.csv). What the data cannot show is whether assignment was randomised, what the blocks were, and which unit was assigned when clusters are small and aliased (about 8% wrong with 10 families). (ii) Inferring the key is circular only if measured columns are allowed. Restricted to design columns, it returns Subject+Days and id+item. (iii) 'Weak where it matters most' is contradicted by my extension (out/exp1b_consequence.csv; 20 schools, 4 reused class labels, class-level treatment, 300 replicates). Where the log-likelihood picked the true model in 38-76% of replicates, the crossed coding gave a Type I error of 1.7-7.7% against 1.3-5.7% for the nested model. Where it picked the truth in 98-100%, the crossed coding gave 13-34%. The outcome is therefore weakest where the consequences are smallest, and the sound reason to exclude it is the outcome-blind principle. The report's own schema also contradicts decision (4): an x-inferred key inside a unit is rejected. It does not enforce decision (3) either: empty estimands, empty variables, no outcome or assigned role, and an empty assignment list all validate (out/schema_probe.tsv).
recommendation_verdicts.change: Keep the structure, with five changes. (a) Infer, with tolerance and 'inferred' wording, the level at which each predictor varies and candidate keys among ID-typed columns. Keep randomisation status, blocks, ID scope, roles, timing and estimands declaration-only. (b) When ID scope is undeclared, report 'ambiguous' together with outcome-free evidence (attribute consistency across outer units, restart numbering), and never recode. (c) Enforce in code, with conformance tests: non-empty estimands, at least one outcome and one assigned role, non-empty assignment, and referential integrity. (d) Record inferred entries as a top-level list of JSON Pointers, or allow ^x- keys in every object. (e) Base the exclusion of outcome-based structure choice on outcome-blindness, not on unreliability.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q4-schema-format
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: I reproduced the report's results: identical hashes for the 6 examples and edge1, identical parsed-table hashes for all 10 fixtures, and the YAML divergences. I also confirmed that PyYAML BaseLoader and R yaml with identity handlers read all 25 test scalars as the same strings, so authoring in YAML read as strings is feasible. Parity is narrower than claimed, though (out/edge_parity_summary.tsv). Five of 8 new declaration edge cases diverge or crash. R errors on non-zero values below 1e-6 in absolute value. Integers beyond 2^53 crash Python's rfc8785 with an uncaught exception, while R rounds them silently. Keys U+FF08 and U+1F600 hash differently because R sorts by code point, whereas JCS requires UTF-16 order. A lone surrogate crashes Python and is accepted by R. Four of 9 table edge cases diverge. With missingValues absent, Python reads '' as null (the Frictionless default) and R keeps ''. '1_000' becomes 1000 in Python and NA in R. '0x1A' becomes 26 in R and an error in Python. 3.2e-06 errors in R. NaN and INF are valid Frictionless numbers, but neither language can canonicalise them. 'Frictionless tools can read the typing' needs three caveats: the default fieldsMatch is 'exact' (every CSV column, in order), an absent type means 'any', and R frictionless 2.0.1 lacks categories. Generating validators from the schema is a further tool for one maintainer to keep up. fastjsonschema 2.22.3, a zero-dependency validator, compiled the schema but ignored dependentRequired, so third-party validators disagree.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Keep canonical JSON, JCS hashing, the Frictionless subset and YAML authoring read as strings. Add normative rules backed by a shared conformance corpus; my 17 edge cases are a starting point. (1) Numbers are limited to integers within ±2^53 and decimals with at most 15 significant digits, or R gets a full ECMAScript formatter tested against the RFC 8785 vectors. (2) Lone surrogates and non-BMP characters in keys are rejected, unless R implements UTF-16 ordering. (3) A strict lexical layer applies the Frictionless defaults: missingValues [""], regexes for integer and number, and explicit NaN/INF tokens stored as strings. (4) Each package gets a hand-written validator that is tested on valid and invalid files with expected error codes, with jsonschema as the CI oracle. Also document the fieldsMatch and categories caveats, and define data_hash as SHA-256 of the raw file bytes.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q4-schema-vocabulary
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: The mapping of fields to catalogue items is sound. Rechecked with jsonschema 4.26.0, the 6 examples validate and the 7 invalid files are rejected as claimed. Several other claims do not hold. 'Unknown keys are errors' is true only outside the table block: a misspelt categoriesOrdered inside a field passes. Misspelt unit names in nested_in and assignment.unit, nested_in cycles, unknown primaryKey columns and unknown estimand terms all pass. Mobility without observation.time passes, although the description says time is required. Observational multisite data are forced to declare an assignment, and the schema_version constant rejects 0.1.1. The vocabulary also has gaps. The Latin-square example declares prime as assigned to subject with time_varying, a stepped-wedge flag misused for within-subject manipulation. Estimands have no outcome field, although ex3 declares two outcomes. observation.unit is used inconsistently: subject for trial rows in ex3, family for child rows in Z11. With 14 blocks, version 0.1.0 is not minimal for one maintainer.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Ship a v0.1 core: table, units (nested_in, id_scope, membership), crossings, observation (key, time), assignment, variables, estimands and provenance. Defer dyad, eeg, imputation and time-zone detail to 0.2 or later. Add assignment.level (between_unit or within_unit), or allow assignment to the observation together with a list column. Add estimand.outcome, and define observation.unit as the unit of one row. Accept any 0.1.x version. Enforce that membership 'may_change_over_time' requires observation.time. Require assignment only for cluster_randomised, stepped_wedge and partially_nested. Add a semantic-validation layer covering references, cycles and columns.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q8-domains
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: Choosing nested education data and crossed subjects x items fits the maintainer's fields and covers nesting versus crossing. I reconfirmed the dataset sizes the report quotes: Hsb82 7,185 rows in 160 schools; fhch2010 13,222 rows, 45 participants and 600 items; stroop 246,600 rows, 685 participants and 4 studies; star 26,796 rows, 80 schools and 1,387 teachers. The claim that public data for both domains reach Python through Rdatasets fails for the crossed domain, however. languageR and afex have 0 entries in Rdatasets, so lexdec, latinsquare, fhch2010 and stroop have no Python route, which leaves only lme4's InstEval and VerbAgg. The only R CRT dataset, mixor::SmokingPrevention, needs R >= 4.6.0 and also has no Python route. Using binary accuracy in the first vignettes conflicts with the proposal's sequencing, which puts GLMMs last, and with statsmodels having no frequentist GLMM; its crossed LMMs are also slow.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Keep the two driving domains. In v0.1, make the crossed vignette Gaussian (log RT) for Stream A and use binary accuracy only in the Stream B audits until GLMMs are supported. Build the CRT and crossed vignettes on zoo fixtures shared byte for byte by both languages, and use the lme4, mlmRev and nlme sets as R-only or Rdatasets-fetched extras. recommendation_verdicts.question: Q8-corpus
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: I reconfirmed every primary source behind the layering. CRAN policy revision 6985 limits data to 5 MB as a general rule, requires graceful failure of Internet resources and requires clear copyright. PyPI's personal defaults are 100 MB per file and 10 GB per project. The Rdatasets README says the data licences could not be determined. ERP CORE is CC BY-SA 4.0. statsmodels' get_rdataset fetches from raw.githubusercontent.com. The four layers follow from these. Caveats: calling the R datasets 'GPL/AGPL material' assumes the package licence covers the data, which Rdatasets says cannot be determined. The erpcore package is itself CC BY 4.0, while ERP CORE data are CC BY-SA 4.0. MNE's mirror holds only a subset of ERP CORE, so the N400 build needs OSF. The licences of the external candidates (OSF 4p8hz, LSHTM, Many Labs 2 project 8cd4r and the openESM datasets) remain unverified.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Keep the four layers. Add REUSE-style licence files per directory so that the root MIT licence is not read as covering corpus data. Record each dataset's licence evidence (URL, date and quoted text) in a corpus manifest. Make the Python examples that fetch from Rdatasets optional documentation that skips on network failure.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q8-zoo

Monte Carlo false-flag and detection rates are informative only for stochastic or thresholded checks; deterministic T0 counts need unit tests, not HPC grids.

missed_considerations: ID scope has outcome-free (T0) evidence beyond label incidence: attribute consistency across outer units (in Exam, 269 of 322 shared student labels change sex across schools; in fhch2010, 0 of 600 items change frequency or length) and restart numbering. Report it as evidence for 'ambiguous', never as a recode.
Separate the level at which treatment varies, which a tolerant rule infers reliably, from randomisation status, unit and blocks, which need a declaration.

Excluding outcome-based structure choice should rest on outcome-blindness. Unreliability is no argument: where the outcome discriminates poorly, choosing wrongly costs at most about 2-3 points of Type I error (exp1b).

The report's own schema contradicts the decisions. x-inferred inside a unit is rejected. Empty estimands, empty variables and an empty assignment pass, and outcome and assigned roles are not enforced. Referential integrity, nested_in cycles, membership requiring time, typos inside table fields and the version constant are all unhandled.
The vocabulary has gaps: assignment within a unit (Latin square, crossover across items), an estimand-to-outcome link, and consistent semantics for observation.unit.

Exact parity needs normative rules for the number domain, keys outside the BMP, lone surrogates and the Frictionless lexical forms (default missingValues, integer and number regexes, NaN/INF), plus a shared conformance corpus. 17 edge cases are provided in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lmecheck/76ff8921-f521-5c13-b469-59b514d4e510/scratchpad/r2/E-verify/edge and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-lmecheck/76ff8921-f521-5c13-b469-59b514d4e510/scratchpad/r2/E-verify/edgezoo.
Frictionless compatibility caveats: the default fieldsMatch 'exact' requires every CSV column, in order; an absent type means 'any'; R frictionless 2.0.1 lacks categories.

Validator strategy for one maintainer: hand-written validators in both languages plus a corpus of valid and invalid files with expected error codes, and jsonschema as the CI oracle. Third-party validators disagree: fastjsonschema missed dependentRequired.

Python has no route to the crossed psycholinguistic datasets (languageR and afex are not in Rdatasets) or to the R CRT dataset (mixor needs R >= 4.6.0, against the proposal's R >= 4.1 floor). Vignettes shared across languages should therefore use zoo fixtures.
A binary-accuracy vignette in v0.1 conflicts with the proposal's GLMM-last sequencing and with statsmodels having no frequentist GLMM.
HPC Monte Carlo validation is needed only for stochastic or thresholded checks. Deterministic T0 counts need unit tests, which cuts ARC time and maintainer effort.
Trim vocabulary 0.1.0 to a core and defer dyad, eeg, imputation and time-zone blocks. Fourteen blocks is not minimal for a single maintainer.

In outcome-blind mode, draft_design() must read values only from ID-typed and right-hand-side columns, never from the formula's left-hand side or from undeclared columns that may be derived from the outcome.
Define data_hash as SHA-256 of the raw bytes for provenance, and keep the parsed-table hash for parity tests only.
Offer a code-first builder API in R and Python that writes the same JSON. The proposal already calls for a structured specification builder for Python users.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q9-venue (software-plus-validation paper and a separate methods paper)
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: Splitting the work into a validation paper and a JOSS paper follows from JOSS policy, which I re-read on 2026-11-07 (docs/submitting.md, paper.md, policies.md, review_criteria.md). The policy forbids papers that focus on research results, allows co-publication if disclosed, charges no fees, sets 750–1,750 words and requires State of the field, Software design, Research impact and AI-usage sections. The reasons for rejecting The R Journal also check out. Four problems remain. (1) F did not consider a Registered Report, although it already recommends preregistration after a pilot. The ADEMP-PreReg authors' wiki (raw.githubusercontent.com/wiki/bsiepe/ADEMP-PreReg/Home.md) lists AMPPS, Behavior Research Methods and BJMSP as journals that accept Registered Reports for simulation studies. Precedents include a Registered Report simulation study in AMPPS and a registered replication of Maas & Hox (2005) on multilevel sample sizes. In-principle acceptance before the HPC runs would protect a sole maintainer if checks turn out 'not assessable', which also makes F's revisit_if branch moot. (2) Psychological Methods as the default first target is weakly supported. The study validates one developer's own implementations, which F itself declares non-neutral, and that weakens any claim to general findings. Psychological Methods is not on the Registered Report list, and its review times were not checked. (3) JOSS for a sole author: the review criteria call 'single author with no evidence of community engagement, external use, or collaborative input' not acceptable and invite reviewers to question a short author list. Research use should therefore come from the maintainer's own substantive analyses, not only from the validation paper. The repository pablobernabeu/lmecheck is still private (created 2026-11-02), so the six-month clock has not started. (4) All facts about JSS, BRM, AMPPS, Psychological Methods and JORS remain unverified, because the publisher hosts are blocked and the shared web-search budget was exhausted in this session.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Paper 1: after the pilot, submit the validation study as a Stage 1 Registered Report to BRM (or AMPPS). Fall back to a preregistered regular BRM article. Target Psychological Methods only if the paper is reframed as a general comparison of diagnostic procedures. Paper 2: JOSS for both packages once the repository has more than 6 months of public history and real research use. Make the repository public now. Keep JSS as the single-paper alternative and drop the AMPPS tutorial until v1.0 is out.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q9-protocol (simulation validation of each check)
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: The protocol is sound in its structure: ADEMP design, Monte Carlo SE arithmetic (all of tables/mcse_targets.csv recomputed correctly), failures counted as outcomes, a declared non-neutral design with comparators, calibration and hold-out halves, and preregistration. All supporting references check out bibliographically. However: (1) The pilot inference about L5-03 is refuted. L5-03 predicts spurious heteroscedasticity in comparisons across cluster sizes. The pilot instead ran a Bartlett test across clusters. My rerun (F-verify/exp/exp3_l503.R, 500 replicates per cell, correct model) gives these false-flag rates for raw conditional residuals compared by size stratum: .068 in F's own pilot cell, .092 and .146 for J = 40 with sizes 2/5/20/50 at ICC .3 and .5, and .182 for J = 100. Studentised residuals give .054–.080, and F's Bartlett operationalisation gives .032–.054. The inflation therefore needs no extreme cells, only the comparison the item names. (2) The plan contradicts itself in several places. V1 runs L5-08/L5-09 influence checks, but the exact deletion refits that L5-08 makes the default (up to 100 levels) are not budgeted; adding them roughly doubles Phase 1 (+1,120 CPU-h). V2-infl uses 200 replicates, so the false-flag MCSE is about .015 against the stated .0049 target. V1 lists Kenward–Roger for n ≤ 400, but the budget omits it, and KR takes 24.7 s per 2×2 maximal fit at 384 rows. V6 lists 3 mismatch levels that the budget does not include, and its 500 × 200 nested design is unnecessary because the prediction depends on design and assumed variances, not on the outer outcome. (3) Engine version affects validity, not only cost. lme4 1.1-38 and later (current 2.1-0, checked in source lmer.R and lmerControl.R) skip derivative-based convergence checks for singular fits, for lmer fits with 10 or more covariance parameters, for glmer fits with 20 or more parameters and for fits with 10,000 or more rows. So V3's engine-flag comparators and the convergence-based stopping rules in V5 behave differently from lme4 1.1-35.1, which every pilot here used. (4) Minor points: the 1.5 × nominal limit is a convention (Bradley's liberal criterion, not verified here) and should be labelled as one. Relative bias is undefined for estimands whose true value is zero. Pass/fail decisions in each of about 300 cells need a smoothing or multiplicity rule.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Operationalise every check exactly as its catalogue item states (statistic, comparison, residual type), and keep L5-03 with studentised residuals. Either budget exact influence refits in V1 or move influence to V2-infl with 2,000 null replicates. Add KR and the V6 mismatch factor to the budget, and run V6 un-nested (design draws × inner simulations once per cell). Pin current engines (lme4 ≥ 2.1-0), record language, engine and version as provenance for each registry threshold, and rerun sentinel cells at each major engine release. Add an absolute-bias criterion for null estimands and use a metamodel or smoothing for per-cell verdicts.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q9-hpc (compute budget and ARC plan)
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed: the ARC facts, re-fetched from oxford-arc on GitHub and byte-identical to F's copies (partitions, defaults, storage, lack of backups, Basic QoS, JobHeldUser and mybalance, the R module, Apptainer). budget.R reproduces F's 1,161, 1,931 and 269 CPU-h exactly. The driver is bit-reproducible and idempotent on this VM. Peak whole-process memory of the largest fits is 236–268 MB, so 2 GB per task is ample. Problems: (1) The central figure uses lme4 1.1-35.1 timings, in which the finite-difference derivative step runs on every fit. With current lme4 defaults, 2×2 maximal lmer fits are 1.9–2.8 times faster: 0.39 vs 0.73 s, 1.47 vs 3.70 s and 8.4 vs 23.3 s at 384, 1,536 and 6,144 rows (deviances identical). The uncapped H1 then costs about 650 CPU-h, close to F's capped 662. The cap therefore loses its cost rationale while dropping the large 2×2 cells where maximal models are most supportable. Combining current lme4, Satterthwaite at 3.1 times a derivative-free fit, KR, allFit with 7 optimisers and an un-nested V6 gives 856 (capped) or 1,137 (uncapped) CPU-h for Phase 1, and up to about 3,050 with exact influence refits (F-verify/tables/budget_sensitivity.csv). That is still far below the claimed 25,000 free core-hours, but that allocation and the Social Sciences Division credit status remain unverified. (2) --constraint='cpu_gen:Cascade_Lake' restricts tasks to htc-c005–c046, about 2,112 cores. The quoted 7,872 cores include GPU nodes (51 of 124), which CPU-only jobs cannot use. The stated rationale also conflicts with arc-systems.rst, which lists the htc interactive nodes htc-g048–049 as Broadwell. (3) The sbatch script rsyncs every completed chunk of the study into each task's $SCRATCH, which wastes I/O for 300-task arrays. (4) The allFit timings cover 5 of 7 optimisers, because optimx and dfoptim are absent here.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Recompute the central budget with lme4 2.1-0 in the HPC-0 calibration and drop the H1 cap (or cut replicates in the large cells instead). Build R libraries in an Apptainer image made off-cluster with portable flags, or on the node type you constrain to, and confirm feature names with sinfo. Check completion against $RESULTS instead of copying the results tree. Pin SimDesign ≥ 2.26 if used: 2.26 fixed a serial-path seed bug that broke runArraySimulation(iseed) reproducibility with parallel = FALSE. If the project's QoS limits concurrency, switch to whole-node multi-core jobs. Archive raw results with a DOI (Zenodo or OSF), since ARC keeps no backups.

recommendation_verdicts.question: Q9-scope (one maintainer)
recommendation_verdicts.reasoning: Tying validation to releases, deferring B's H4, H8 and H10, and prioritising education-relevant modules are proportionate. The claim that compute is not the binding constraint holds in every scenario I ran (Phase 1 between 820 and 3,051 CPU-h). The month-based timeline is optimistic. It assumes simulation infrastructure, pilot and preregistration by month 3 and Phase 1 plus v1.0 by month 6. But the Gaussian Stream A checks must first be implemented in both languages and frozen at a git tag before preregistration and before V1/V2 can run. The timeline also ignores journal review time: a Stage 1 review, or a Psychological Methods rejection followed by BRM, can each take months. The plan does not budget the maintainer's time for re-validating after engine releases, although lme4 changed its convergence-check rules within the last year.
recommendation_verdicts.change: Gate the work on milestones, not months: repository public now; checks implemented and frozen (v0.9 tag); pilot; Stage 1 Registered Report or OSF preregistration; Phase 1 runs; v1.0 with Stage 2 submission; JOSS after more than 6 months of public history and real research use; Phase 2 (GLMM) only after v1.0. Keep a small sentinel validation subset in CI or on HPC for engine updates.

missed_considerations: Registered Report route for the validation paper: the ADEMP-PreReg wiki lists AMPPS, BRM and BJMSP as accepting Registered Reports for simulation studies, with an AMPPS precedent and a registered replication of Maas & Hox (2005). A Stage 1 report fits the preregistration F already recommends and secures publication whatever the results.

Engine-version validity: lme4 ≥ 1.1-38 (current 2.1-0) skips derivative-based convergence checks for singular fits, for lmer fits with 10 or more covariance parameters, for glmer fits with 20 or more parameters and for fits with 10,000 or more rows. Convergence-warning comparators (V3) and stopping rules (V5/H1) must be validated on current engines. Store the engine version as registry provenance and rerun sentinel cells on major releases.

The L5-03 pilot tested the wrong comparison. By cluster-size stratum, raw conditional residuals give false-flag rates of .09–.18 at nominal .05 (F-verify/out/exp3_l503.csv). The protocol must fix each check's exact statistic before any pilot is interpreted.

The protocol and budget disagree: exact influence refits (L5-08) are in V1 but not budgeted (+1,120 CPU-h); KR is listed but not costed; the V6 mismatch factor is missing and V6 is needlessly nested; V2-infl's 200 replicates miss the stated MCSE target. See F-verify/tables/budget_sensitivity.csv.

With current lme4 the H1 cap saves little (uncapped about 650 CPU-h) and removes the large 2×2 designs. Inference cost on selected rungs (Satterthwaite or KR) is missing from both B's and F's H1 estimates.

Cascade Lake constraint: it limits tasks to about 2,112 htc cores, the quoted 7,872 cores include GPU-only nodes, and the htc interactive build nodes are Broadwell. A portable Apptainer build avoids the illegal-instruction problem the constraint was meant to prevent.
The array driver copies the study's entire results tree into every task's $SCRATCH. Check completion against $DATA instead.
If SimDesign is used, pin ≥ 2.26: earlier versions were not reproducible on the serial (1-core) path with iseed.

The GitHub repository is still private (created 2026-11-02), so the JOSS six-month clock has not started. JOSS scrutinises single-author projects and requires evidence of research use beyond a paper about the tool itself.
Archive code and raw replicate results with a DOI (Zenodo or OSF), as JSS/BRM replication rules expect; ARC keeps no backups.
Python-side operating characteristics rest only on the V7 parity subset. Registry thresholds should state the language and engine they were validated in.
Contingency if the project's QoS limits concurrency (as Basic QoS does): switch to whole-node multi-core jobs.
The month-based timeline needs replacing with milestone gates. Preregistration requires frozen check code in both languages, and journal and Stage 1 review times are not included.
